items.title: Estuary sails into kidney disease space with $103M for gene therapies
items.snippet: Estuary Biotherapeutics is seeking to address the root cause of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with two gene therapy programs based on science from Yale.

items.title: City’s IPO soars to $200M, with proceeds supporting thromboembolic disease pipeline
items.snippet: City Therapeutics will join a slew of biotechs that have entered the public markets this year, with a $200 million raise that landed above expectations.

items.title: FDA issues warning over Eurofins’ selective recording that 'compromises' data
items.snippet: Inconsistent reporting at a Pennsylvania site affected microbiological analyses of components and drug products that analytical testing service provider Eurofins ran for customers.

items.title: OrbiMed raises two new life sciences funds worth $3B with one aiming for Asia
items.snippet: The sixth cycle of OrbiMed’s Asia Partners fund included one with more than $1 billion earmarked for life science companies based on the Eastern continent.

items.title: iPSCs come of age, powering breakthroughs in the lab and clinic
items.snippet: After years of quiet maturation, new approach methodologies and emerging clinical success for cell therapies are fueling parallel momentum for induced pluripotent stem cells.

items.title: AstraZeneca bulks up MASH, cardio work in up to $1.5B AI partnership with insitro
items.snippet: AstraZeneca will tap AI-focused insitro to find new targets for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and cardiomyopathies, following the Phase 3 failure of its Ionis-partnered Wainua in transthyretin-mediated amyloid cardiomyopathy.

items.title: Webinar: The China question: Can US biotechs lead as investment heads east?
items.snippet: In this webinar, BioSpace will gathered experts to discuss China’s impact on the future of biotech and how both U.S. and Chinese companies can thrive—and maybe even collaborate.

items.title: GSK laying off 1.2K+ in Belgium
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: FDA's latest rare disease framework seeks to prioritize consistency in flexibility
items.snippet: Following several recent initiatives, the FDA's newest rare disease framework sets out to standardize the agency's approach to scientific evidence and bring rare disease therapies to patients faster.

items.title: Stoffels strikes up new biotech in return to Galapagos cell therapy mission
items.snippet: A new biotech co-founded by Paul Stoffels has formed to take on the CAR T cell assets of Galapagos almost a year after the company—now known as Lakefront Biotherapeutics—abandoned them.

items.title: Arrowhead’s blood-brain barrier tech is ‘arguably better’ than others, analysts say after data drop
items.snippet: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals’ siRNA candidate achieved “compelling” tau reductions in an early study of healthy volunteers, with a magnitude of effect that seems to outperformother blood-brain barrier platforms, according to Stifel.

items.title: Vanda freezes Novartis-originated social anxiety program after late-stage disappointment
items.snippet: While Oppenheimer doesn’t see the Phase 3 stumble of VQW-765 as highly detrimental to Vanda Pharmaceuticals, the analyst nevertheless believes the stakes are now higher for the company’s planned Q4 readout for Nereus in GLP-1-induced vomiting.

items.title: The decisions behind scientific progress
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, presented by Cytiva, Jennifer Smith-Parker speaks to Nicolas Pivet, VP & GM, Manufacturing & Digital Solutions at Cytiva. In this episode, we explore how biopharma’s real bottleneck isn’t too little data—it’s too little confidence in the decisions that drive development, manufacturing and...

items.title: Gilead snags equity stake in Vir with up to $1.87B deal for three T cell engagers
items.snippet: The Gilead Sciences deal, which include $135 million in upfront and near-term payments, marks a critical platform validation for Vir Biotechnology as investors await an upcoming readout in solid tumors.

items.title: Verastem reports ‘robust’ response rate in pancreatic cancer subgroup where Rasonque struggled
items.snippet: Revolution Medicines’ recently approved drug showed a 24% overall response rate and a high rate of side effects in patients whose cancer has a G12D mutation, reinforcing Mizuho’s view that a more specific agent such as Verastem Oncology’s VS-7375 “should come first for G12D patients.”

items.title: ‘Pharma bro’ Shkreli runs afoul of court’s lifetime pharma ban
items.snippet: Since his release from prison in 2022, Martin Shkreli has traded stocks and publicly opined on news events, damaging reputations and sinking share prices for small biotechs including Capricor and Cassava, the FTC alleges.

items.title: GSK plans 1.2K+ layoffs at Belgium sites as $2.5B restructure gains momentum
items.snippet: The layoffs across GSK’s Belgium sites come on the heels of the pharma’s planned shuttering of its German vaccine manufacturing site, which prompted job cuts for about 650 employees.

items.title: Zealand pens up to $1.2B deal with Generate for AI-designed obesity, metabolic drugs
items.snippet: Obesity-focused Zealand Pharma is buying into Generate:Biomedicines’s generative AI platform to create new multispecific drug candidates.

items.title: Verdiva ends mid-stage study of oral GLP-1 amid ‘market evolution’
items.snippet: The candidate is an oral version of ecnoglutide, a subcutaneous formulation of which is approved in China for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Pfizer owns commercialization rights for ecnoglutide in the Asian country.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
